A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PNLAC/InhibitFT study. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–B are readable and can be matched despite substantial reformatting.

before.justification: v1 reports original neuron-localization, activation-patching, fine-tuning, and ablation results across four LLMs, including extensive appendix results.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and their numerical and graphical results in the main text and Appendix B.

M1.justification: Section 5(b) changes from fine-tuning 'topic-specific neurons and other neurons' to only topic-specific neurons. However, both versions already say 'only topic-specific' elsewhere and retain the same general-neuron gradient masking. Whether this changes the procedure or merely cleans up inconsistent wording is unresolved. PAS renames the existing activation score.

E1.justification: Both versions use IDEOINST's six political topics, Political Compass, and IDRlabs Ideologies Test for the same political-stance tasks. The appendices introduce no additional coverage.

E2.justification: The evaluated comparators remain standard right-leaning fine-tuning and random-neuron InhibitFT in Table 1, Tables 4–6, and the corresponding figures. Vanilla-model and activation-patching comparisons are also retained.

E3.justification: The reported evaluation settings retain the same four model configurations, 100 IDEOINST validation questions per topic, GPT-4o-mini stance judge, RMSE/CoLA/MNLI metrics, and eight selection thresholds from 2.5% to 25%. No new evaluation protocol is reported.

E4.justification: Both retain the neuron-distribution analyses, general versus topic-specific activation-patching tests, random-freezing control, and threshold ablation in Section 5.2 and Tables 7–10. No supplementary analysis is added or removed.

E5.justification: Both report point estimates without repeated-run counts, seed information, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. v2 adds no statistical uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: All 1,880 score entries in Tables 1–10 match. For example, Table 1 retains Crime RMSE values of 0.847 for standard fine-tuning and 0.433 for InhibitFT on Llama-3.1-8B. The plotted results and reported mitigation figures are also unchanged.

T1.justification: Equation 1, the neuron-set definitions, and the RMSE formula in Appendix B.2 remain mathematically unchanged. Naming the activation score PAS introduces no new definition, derivation, or proof.

C1.justification: v2's abstract specifies middle and later layers for neuron localization, and contribution 1 explicitly presents PAS as a new metric. The central claims about two neuron types, approximately 20% mitigation, and a sufficient 5% neuron subset remain unchanged.

C2.justification: New Section 7 acknowledges potentially incomplete or imprecise identification of general political neurons across the six topics and limitations of AI-based evaluation without human assessment. These specific qualifications are absent from v1; the existing result interpretations remain.

D1.justification: Appendices A–B retain the prompt templates, single L20 48GB GPU, six epochs, batch size eight, learning rate 2 × 10^-5, and 5% selection setting. IDEOINST provenance moves from Section 3.1 to Appendix A.1; access information is unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 substantially expands cited coverage with 17 added works spanning reasoning, reliability, value neurons, cross-lingual privacy, representation steering, sycophancy, and circuit discovery. It removes Aly et al. (2025) and Guo et al. (2025). The central research-gap claim about political-stance mechanisms remains.

P1.justification: Localized edits introduce PAS terminology, rename Section 3, consolidate the detailed IDEOINST description in Appendix A.1, update affiliations, and add a limitations section. Most explanatory prose and the overall argument structure are retained.

P2.justification: The document undergoes extensive reformatting of typography, columns, and figure/table sizes and placement. Table captions move above tables, appendix example boxes receive colored styling, and Figure 1's caption expands. All twelve figures and ten tables are retained.

improvement.justification: New Section 7 improves transparency about neuron-identification coverage and reliance on AI judges without human validation. Clearer terminology and Figure 1's expanded caption also help exposition. The gain is limited: empirical and statistical support remain unchanged, the training-description ambiguity persists, and several result displays become smaller.
